title: One dashboard for a whole homelab

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ten browser tabs open: one for your media server, one for your downloader, one for your container manager. Your RAM is crying. What if they all lived on one page?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That sounds like a dream for anyone with a homelab. Is that what this is?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It is. DasherControl is Antoine's dashboard for dockerized web apps, built with Vue on the front and Rust with Rocket on the back. Think of a desktop of widgets, like Windows Vista gadgets, but on the web and saved in a database.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So how do the apps show up?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Each widget is a grid item, and he calls them applets. An applet can wrap a site in an iframe, hold a bookmark, or do a daily homelab task. Apps like Sonarr and Jellyfin sit side by side on one screen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. You can save a workspace, switch between workspaces, and manage your applets. There's also user authentication, so the dashboard has a front door.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It has a simple container controller, so you can start and manage Docker containers from the same place. The whole thing installs with Docker or Docker Compose, in keeping with the idea that everything is a web app in a container.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Tools like Portainer or the Docker command line work, but putting a reverse proxy with SSL in front of everything takes time. Antoine wanted small applets for the things he does every day when managing his homelab.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The roadmap lists theme and background customization, canvas applets, a web SSH terminal, OAuth login with GitHub, and a Caddy config generator for reverse proxy and SSL. Floating windows are on the list too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A lot of ideas for one dashboard.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It is a playground for his homelab ideas. The project page has a demo animation, and the GitHub repository has the full roadmap and install steps.
